name: London System
openings: Queen's Pawn Game: Accelerated London System
summary: 1.d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3 and c3: White builds the same solid setup against almost every Black defence. The bishop leaves before e3 shuts it in, the pawns on c3, d4 and e3 hold the centre, and a knight on e5 with f4 and Bd3 leads to a kingside attack. The course also covers how Black fights it with ...c5 and ...Qb6, and the b2 pawn the early bishop leaves behind.

white: Play Bf4 before e3, so the dark-squared bishop is outside the pawn chain.
Build the pyramid c3, d4, e3: if Black takes on d4, recapture with a pawn and keep the centre.
Put a knight on e5, support it with f4, and aim the d3 bishop at h7 for a kingside attack.
Meet ...Bd6 with Bg3: if Black takes, hxg3 opens the h-file for the rook.
Remember b2: once the bishop leaves c1, answer ...Qb6 at once with Qb3, Nc3 or c4.
black: Hit d4 from the side with ...c5 and ...Nc6, and the b2 pawn with ...Qb6.
Gain queenside space with ...c4 when White's queen or bishop must move.
Offer to trade the f4 bishop with ...Bd6: it is White's best minor piece.
Keep a knight ready for ...Nxe5 or ...f6 so the e5 knight cannot stay forever.

structures.name: The pyramid: c3, d4, e3 against d5, e6
structures.text: White's pawns form a triangle that is very hard to break. The f4 bishop sits outside it. Black's main break is ...c5; White meets ...cxd4 with exd4 and keeps a pawn on d4. The e5 square is White's outpost.

structures.name: Stonewall grip: Ne5 with f4
structures.text: When the knight lands on e5 and the f-pawn comes to f4, ...Nxe5 is met by fxe5, which opens the f-file for White's rook. The plan is Rf3 or Qf3 and g4-g5 against Black's king.

structures.name: The open h-file after ...Bxg3 hxg3
structures.text: Black wins the bishop pair, but White's h1 rook gets a half-open file toward h7. Black castling short then faces the d3 bishop, the rook and a queen on the h-file.

structures.name: Against ...g6: the same setup, a different target
structures.text: Against the King's Indian setup the f4 bishop takes e5 from Black's ...e5 push. White plays h3 so the bishop can retreat to h2 when ...Nh5 hits it.

white: f4 bishop: the London's signature piece. It controls e5 and c7 and retreats to g3 or h2, never back to c1.
d3 bishop: aims at h7. Against ...g6 it goes to e2 instead.
f3 knight: jumps to e5; the d2 knight then takes its place on f3.
d2 knight: guards e4 and keeps the c-pawn free to go to c3.
Queen: Qb3 or Qc1 against ...Qb6; Qe2 or Qf3 when the attack starts.
black: c-pawn: ...c5 hits d4; ...c4 gains space and takes d3 from White's bishop.
Queen: ...Qb6 hits b2, the pawn the f4 bishop no longer guards.
Dark-squared bishop: ...Bd6 offers to trade White's f4 bishop.
Light-squared bishop: ...Bb7 or ...Bf5, outside the pawn chain.

lines.name: Main setup: Ne5 and f4 against ...e6 and ...c5
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 c5 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 7. Bg3 O-O 8. Bd3 b6 9. Ne5 Bb7 10. f4

notes.1.d4: Takes the centre and opens a path for the c1 bishop.
notes.2.Nf3: Develops toward the centre and guards d4 and e5.
notes.3.Bf4: The London bishop: it leaves before e3 shuts it in, and it controls e5.
notes.4.e3: Supports d4 and opens the f1 bishop's diagonal.
notes.4...c5: Black's main break: it attacks d4 from the side.
notes.5.c3: The pyramid c3, d4, e3. If ...cxd4, White retakes with the e-pawn and keeps a pawn on d4.
notes.6.Nbd2: The knight guards e4 and can go to f3 when the other knight jumps to e5. On c3 it would block the c-pawn.
notes.6...Bd6: Offers to trade the f4 bishop, White's best minor piece.
notes.7.Bg3: Keeps the bishop. If ...Bxg3, hxg3 opens the h-file for the h1 rook.
notes.8.Bd3: Aims at h7, the weak point in front of Black's castled king.
notes.8...b6: Prepares ...Bb7 on the long diagonal; once the c6 knight moves, the bishop guards d5.
notes.9.Ne5: The outpost: only ...f6 can attack e5 with a pawn. The knight hits c6, d7, f7 and g4.
notes.10.f4: Supports the knight with a pawn. If ...Nxe5, fxe5 opens the f-file. Next come Rf3 or Qf3 and g4.

lines.name: ...c5 and ...Qb6: Black hits b2
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 c5 4. e3 Nc6 5. c3 Qb6 6. Qb3 c4 7. Qc2 Bf5 8. Qc1 e6 9. Nbd2 h6 10. Be2

notes.3...c5: Black attacks d4 at once, before White's setup is complete.
notes.5.c3: Supports d4, so ...cxd4 is met by exd4.
notes.5...Qb6: The queen hits b2. The bishop that guarded b2 from c1 is now on f4.
notes.6.Qb3: Guards b2 and offers a queen trade. After ...Qxb3 axb3 the a-file opens for White's rook.
notes.6...c4: Black chases the queen with tempo and gains space on the queenside.
notes.7...Bf5: Develops outside the pawn chain and hits the queen again.
notes.8.Qc1: The queen guards b2 from c1 and stays off the bishop's diagonal.
notes.9.Nbd2: Prepares b3 or e4 to break up Black's pawn on c4.
notes.9...h6: Gives the f5 bishop the h7 square, safe from Nh4.
notes.10.Be2: Not Bd3: the c4 pawn controls d3. This is Black's most active answer to the London, and White must play carefully.

lines.name: ...Bd6 and ...Bxg3: the open h-file
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 Bd6 5. Bg3 Bxg3 6. hxg3 O-O 7. Bd3 c5 8. Ne5 h6 9. c3 Qb6 10. Qe2 Nc6 11. f4

notes.4...Bd6: Black challenges the f4 bishop at once.
notes.5.Bg3: White keeps the bishop on the diagonal. If Black trades, White recaptures toward the centre.
notes.6.hxg3: The h-file opens for the h1 rook, which now aims at h7. The g3 pawn guards f4.
notes.7.Bd3: The bishop and the rook both aim at h7.
notes.8.Ne5: The knight takes the outpost before White castles.
notes.8...h6: Takes g5 from White's pieces, but the pawn on h6 now stands on the half-open h-file, in front of the h1 rook.
notes.9.c3: Guards d4 again before Black's pieces arrive.
notes.9...Qb6: Hits b2, the pawn the bishop no longer guards.
notes.10.Qe2: Guards b2 along the second rank and keeps castling long open.
notes.11.f4: Now ...Nxe5 is met by fxe5. White plans g4 and g5 against the h6 pawn.

lines.name: Against ...g6: h3 and a quiet centre
lines.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. Bf4 Bg7 4. e3 d6 5. h3 O-O 6. Be2 c5 7. c3 Nc6 8. O-O

notes.2...g6: Black puts the bishop on g7, as in the King's Indian.
notes.3.Bf4: The bishop controls e5, the square Black's ...e5 push needs.
notes.5.h3: Gives the bishop the h2 square. If ...Nh5 hits it, Bh2 keeps it on the same diagonal.
notes.6.Be2: On d3 the bishop would hit the solid g6 pawn, so it goes to e2.
notes.6...c5: Black hits d4 from the side.
notes.7.c3: The pyramid again: if ...cxd4, exd4 keeps the centre.
notes.8.O-O: The king is safe; White plays Nbd2 next and keeps e5 under control.

lines.name: Accelerated London: 2.Bf4 first
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3 e6 4. Nf3 Bd6 5. Bg3 O-O 6. Bd3 c5 7. Nbd2 Nc6 8. c3 b6 9. Ne5

notes.2.Bf4: The bishop comes out at once, before Nf3: the setup is the same, only the move order changes.
notes.3.e3: With the bishop outside the chain, e3 supports d4 at no cost.
notes.4.Nf3: The usual setup is complete in a different order.
notes.4...Bd6: Offers to trade the f4 bishop.
notes.5.Bg3: Keeps the bishop; ...Bxg3 hxg3 would open the h-file for White.
notes.6.Bd3: Aims at h7 after Black has castled.
notes.7.Nbd2: Guards e4 and keeps c3 free for the pawn.
notes.8.c3: The pyramid c3, d4, e3 is complete.
notes.9.Ne5: The knight takes the outpost; f4 can follow, as in the main setup.

traps.name: 5.Qd2?: the queen that does not guard b2
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 c5 4. e3 Qb6 5. Qd2 Qxb2 6. c3 Qxa1

notes.3.Bf4: The bishop leaves c1, so nothing guards b2.
notes.5.Qd2: The mistake: the queen seems to guard b2, but the c2 pawn stands between them.

traps.punishment: 5...Qxb2 hits the a1 rook and the b1 knight together. White cannot guard both, and after 6.c3 Qxa1 Black has won a rook and a pawn, and the queen gets out. Answer ...Qb6 with 5.Nc3 or 5.c4, which give b2 only for quick development, or with Qb3 once c3 is played.

traps.name: 4...Qxb2?: the poisoned b-pawn
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 c5 3. e3 Qb6 4. Nc3 Qxb2 5. Nxd5

notes.2.Bf4: The Accelerated London: the bishop comes out before Nf3.
notes.4.Nc3: White offers the b-pawn: the knight now eyes d5 and b5.
notes.4...Qxb2: The mistake: the queen goes far from home and nothing guards c7.

traps.punishment: 5.Nxd5 threatens Nc7+, forking the king and the a8 rook, and Rb1 chases the queen. For example 5...Nf6 6.Rb1 Qxa2 7.Nc7+ Kd8 8.Nxa8, and White wins a rook. Develop with 4...Nf6 instead.
